# Per-binding FFI overhead

<!-- Generated by `node tools/comparison/dist/perf/overhead-table.js` from the records under `results/counts/ab/`; `mise run verify:claims` fails if it drifts from them. Do not edit by hand. -->

What each binding layer adds to an operation over the Rust core, as retired user-space instructions (`instructions:u`) per operation: the median over the record's interleaved A B / B A blocks of `mise run benchmark:counts`. Arm A is the layer's driver and arm B the core's, built in the same crate and profile from `bindings/overhead/protocol.rs`; both arms' outputs are byte-identical in every record. Every cell is tier 1 on the perf matrix's gradient fixture; a batch is 16 copies through a one-worker batch encoder. No wall-clock figure is recorded or claimed. Reproduce with `mise run benchmark:overhead`.

## Host runtimes

What each host runtime adds to a call, counted through its published binding. Arm A is the host's own command-line driver (the cross-language benchmark's `encode-stdin`), run under the host's counting configuration (`counts-core.ts` `COUNTING_CONFIGS`); arm B is the core driver of the native layer the host binds, counted with `--b-impl Rust` on the same cell, and both arms decode to the same RGBA bytes or encode to the same hash in every record. A host is countable where, in every one of its records, each arm's per-operation count in each of the interleaved blocks is within 1.000% of that arm's median; the check and its tolerance were fixed in issue #173 before any host was counted. The check tests that a record repeats, not that its per-operation figure is independent of the iteration count: work a process does once, part-way through the long process only (a JIT compile at its call threshold, say), is spread over the iterations, so each figure is its cell's at that record's iteration count (`settings.iterations`). Kotlin is counted in the JVM's interpreter for this reason; with C1 at its call threshold its decode counted about 12% more per call at 500 iterations than at 2,000. In the interpreter a smaller dependence remains, unexplained: arm A counts 0.5% more per decode at 500 iterations than at 2,000, 0.9% more per 64×64 encode at 200 than at 800, and 0.7% more per 512×512 encode at 20 than at 80, where the core (arm B) also moves by 0.1% and the host side falls by about 13%. A counting configuration is not how the host ships: it pins the runtime's compiler tier and its collector's pacing, so a host's figure is its cost under that configuration. "Native layer" is the overhead row above for the same cell, counted against the same core binary, and "Host side" is what is left: the host's call, its marshalling and its runtime, with its CLI's bench loop. The TypeScript (wasm) arm runs the core itself as wasm in V8's baseline compiler, so its figure is the whole call against native code rather than the glue alone; the glue's share is not separable by this count.

| Go | `GOGC=off` `GOMAXPROCS=1` | 0.099% | yes |

## Every binding

| Binding | Native layer | Counted here | Not counted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C | C ABI | the whole call | — |
| C# | C ABI | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | the .NET runtime (tiered JIT, concurrent collector) as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| Go | C ABI | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | the Go runtime (its concurrent collector, every processor) as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| Kotlin/JVM | UniFFI scaffolding | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | the JVM (tiered C1/C2 compilation in the background, its default collector) as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| Android | UniFFI scaffolding | the native side of every call, as Kotlin/JVM | JNA and ART: they run on a device, not on the counting host |
| Python | UniFFI scaffolding | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | CPython started through `uv run`, with a random hash seed as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| TypeScript (wasm) | wasm-bindgen | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | V8 with its optimizing tiers (Maglev, TurboFan) and background threads, which is where the wasm core runs as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| Swift | UniFFI scaffolding | not measured | Swift builds on macOS only (`ci-swift.yml`); its native layer is the UniFFI row above |

## Reductions

Each reduction is byte-identical (both arms' outputs are equal in every record) and is shown by a paired count of the layer's driver after it (A) against the same driver built before it (B), each cell counted with `benchmark:overhead`'s options, `--impl` naming the driver's implementation and `--b-bin` naming the earlier build; every block of every record counts fewer instructions after it.

### `uniffi-bytes` (uniffi)

UniFFI byte arrays lifted and lowered in one slice copy instead of one push per byte (`bindings/uniffi/src/bytes.rs`); `ImageInput.rgba` lifted straight into the core's `Arc<[u8]>`. B is `bindings/uniffi/target/before/overhead_uniffi`, built at `c4b3f9e`.

| Cell | After (A) | Before (B) | Change | A/B | Record |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| encode 64×64 | 3,740,198 | 4,345,106 | −604,908 per encode | 0.8608 | `reduce-uniffi-bytes-encode-64.json` |
| encode 512×512 | 109,947,533 | 148,321,668 | −38,374,135 per encode | 0.7413 | `reduce-uniffi-bytes-encode-512.json` |
| decode (64×64's hash) | 2,405,443 | 2,450,508 | −45,065 per decode | 0.9816 | `reduce-uniffi-bytes-decode-64.json` |
| batch of 16 × 64×64 | 59,868,230 | 69,598,781 | −9,730,551 per batch | 0.8602 | `reduce-uniffi-bytes-batch16-64.json` |

### `wasm-rgba-copy` (wasm)

`DecodeResult::rgba` returns a `Uint8Array` built from the decoded slice (`bindings/wasm/src/lib.rs`), so the pixels cross to JS in one copy instead of a clone in the wasm heap, wasm-bindgen's copy of the clone and its free. Counted through the TypeScript package's CLI under Node's counting configuration (Host runtimes), on the decode cell, the only one whose path it changes. B is `bindings/wasm/target/before/typescript/dist/encode-stdin.js`, built at `4fd0571`.

| Cell | After (A) | Before (B) | Change | A/B | Record |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| decode (64×64's hash) | 6,128,083 | 6,129,710 | −1,627 per decode | 0.9997 | `reduce-wasm-rgba-copy-decode-64.json` |

### `uniffi-py-bytes` (uniffi)

The Python bindings write a byte array into the RustBuffer in one `ctypes.memmove` instead of one Python loop iteration per byte, by a step `mise run cbuild:python` applies to uniffi-bindgen's output (`mise-tasks/cbuild/python`), so lowering `ImageInput.rgba` no longer runs w × h × 4 iterations per encode. Counted through the Python package's CLI under CPython's counting configuration (Host runtimes), on the encode cells, the ones whose input it writes; each arm is a package directory, run from its parent. B is `bindings/uniffi/target/before/python/chromahash`, built at `32ffc24`.

| Cell | After (A) | Before (B) | Change | A/B | Record |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| encode 64×64 | 3,729,075 | 46,326,177 | −42,597,102 per encode | 0.0805 | `reduce-uniffi-py-bytes-encode-64.json` |
| encode 512×512 | 107,109,034 | 2,833,081,139 | −2,725,972,105 per encode | 0.0379 | `reduce-uniffi-py-bytes-encode-512.json` |

Counted at 84e33389d9258cbebac4f536fe8a1accd9613278, 8f78dff892aebb1882d0e4a25a94e04a29eb830c, b2f222f6f7748e404fc21d1cdf9b99df8dcd18cf, baa863e782fbce9d3437875241b86717131a52c4 on AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor; each record holds its binaries' SHA-256, the host, the counter and every block.
